producer_report.summary: Low disk after the build no longer closes a job failed. At the gate before the checks and the gate before the verifier, the new `Athena::hold_for_disk` (run/close.rs) commits the attempt's records with no Score and no Outcome, writes the hold marker with the free and required amounts, removes the verifier snapshot, keeps the job's resume mark and returns `LowDisk`. `push_closing_records` is now shared with `close_dispatched`. The job stays Dispatched with no process, so it reads as interrupted: no failure, introspection, failure class or scope-guard attempt. The drain already maps `LowDisk` to a held item with no attempt used. On a later pass it lists the job as interrupted and calls `Athena::retry` itself, which resumes from the kept candidate with no planner or producer run. So "no `athena retry`" means no person runs it; D146 says so. The resume skips the rebuild only while main has changed nothing outside records/; the docs, D146 and CHANGELOG state this. A failed write probe at the verifier gate is held with free = 0 and the probe error printed first (`verifier_environment_problem` now returns `Option<LowDisk>`; `before_verifier_reason` is deleted). Status fills the hold for an interrupted job and display says the next drain resumes it. Earlier findings: the stale scope_guard test is rewritten (go returns LowDisk, no attempt, then the retry lands as resumed and Accepted), and the D146 entry in docs/decisions.md uses no supersession phrase, so the backtest passes. The full `cargo test --locked -q` run finished with exit code 0, as did fmt, clippy and the policy scan.

open_issues: The first version of my binary status test called `repo_state_dir` with ATHENA_STATE_DIR unset in the test process, so one stray state directory for a temp repository was written under the default Athena state root, outside my working directory. I could not remove it from here. The test now builds its state path under the fixture's own temp dir, so it no longer leaks. The stray directory has the name of a temp repo dir plus a 12-character key.
The held job stays Dispatched after the retry resumes it, as any interrupted job does today; closing it is out of scope. The retry lists it as its source, so the drain does not retry it twice.
In the still-short drain scenario a single pass may meet the new held job again as queued work, so a pass can print two held lines. Both are holds and no attempt is used; the test allows this.

The Display text of `LowDisk` still says `the job stays queued and is not rejected: free disk space, then run it again`, which is loosely worded for a held, dispatched job. I did not change it because it is shared by the dispatch hold.
mistakes: My first binary status test called repo_state_dir without ATHENA_STATE_DIR set, which wrote a state directory outside the fixture (see open_issues). Fixed in the test.
My first still-short drain test asserted exactly one job line in pass 2; the drain meets the new held job again in the same pass. I loosened it to require that every line is a hold.
learnings: The drain already treats LowDisk as a held item with no attempt, and steward::interrupted_work lists a Dispatched job with no process, so the hold needed no new drain path.
Resume (resume_seed) requires pinned.is_none() and no non-records/ change between the job's base and head; the hold and resume tests use a change-capability reading, not a study.
The spawned binary's state directory is $ATHENA_STATE_DIR/<repo-dir-name>-<12-char key>, not the fixture's `repo` directory; a test that shares state with it must use that name.
Plain `grep`, `sed`, `tail` and file reads outside the working directory are blocked for the producer; use the Grep, Read and Glob tools for files inside it.
clippy denies `[x.clone()]` in assert_eq on slices (cloned_ref_to_slice_refs); use std::slice::from_ref.
desires: A way to read a background command's output file from inside the working directory, to see the full-suite result without waiting for the notification.
